title: Forces of Nature
description: Weather, wind, and the untamed growth of the wildsea - elemental hazards that reshape a scene or interrupt a journey.
inPlay: Most forces of nature work best as a condition layered onto another scene, or as a brief interruption to a journey. Their value is the change they force in behaviour - what tasks and actions become harder, and how the NPCs around them react.

basic.name: Branch-Sway
basic.summary: The ceaseless shifting of branches driven by high winds and the excess life in the ironroots; in the wrong moment it can turn a simple wavewalk into disaster.

basic.name: High-Altitude Winds
basic.summary: The surface air is rarely still, and when winds gather force they make traversal treacherous, especially for anyone moving outside a ship.

basic.name: Rapid Growth
basic.summary: Crezzerin instability sends trees into flurries of hyper-accelerated growth, choking clear spaces with new branches and vines within minutes.

hazards.name: A Surge of Burst and Bloom
hazards.summary: A rolling explosion of flower and blossom across the waves, strong enough to catch ships and creatures and carry them along - use it to move the crew from place to place at speed.

hazards.name: Lung-Rooting Danger
hazards.summary: A thick cloud of fungal spores drifting across the surface or through the branches beneath, rewarding clever survival and urgent decisions over open combat.

hazards.name: Rotten, Pale Expanses
hazards.summary: A wood-rot that strips the great trees of their structural integrity and bleaches whole forests white; traversing blanched waves without care is a recipe for destruction.

hazards.name: A Spreading Suffusion of Growth
hazards.summary: Crezzerin, the chemical that drives the wildsea's titanic and endless growth, found in dangerous concentration wherever it courses through sap, rain, and mutated flesh.

hazards.name: The Wrong Kind of Wild
hazards.summary: Flame in a world that is overwhelmingly vegetative, high in oxygen, and primed to burn - unkept fire can destroy anything and everything in its path.

hazards.name: Tunnels to the Under-Eaves
hazards.summary: A rift in the waves, a yawning chasm that can lead all the way down to the Under-Eaves. Most animals avoid them, and crews would do well to follow their lead.
